item.title: CISA adds Linux Kernel Fragnesia vulnerability CVE-2026-121980 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, enforcing an emergency remediation mandate for an actively weaponized Linux kernel vulnerability. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit memory fragmentation subroutines to crash target hosts or execute arbitrary kernel-level code.
The emergency directive covers Linux kernel vulnerability CVE-2026-121980 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8 and codenamed Fragnesia. The security flaw resides within IPv6 packet fragmentation reassembly routines in kernel network stacks. Unauthenticated remote adversaries send malformed IPv6 packet sequences to trigger out-of-bounds heap memory corruption, bypassing kernel address space layout randomization KASLR and executing arbitrary kernel commands. CISA set a mandatory December 7 compliance deadline for Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to deploy updated kernel builds across enterprise cloud infrastructure and edge routing nodes.
Subverting core operating system kernel space presents immediate systemic risks to enterprise cloud workloads, container host clusters, and edge infrastructure. Because the Linux kernel handles core system scheduling, memory management, and network transit, an unauthenticated kernel RCE permits threat actors to compromise host hypervisors, extract container secrets, and break tenant isolation boundaries.
- Update Linux kernel installations immediately across server fleets to patched long-term support release builds. - Restrict inbound IPv6 fragment processing at edge firewalls and cloud network security groups where IPv6 fragmentation is not required. - Inspect system kernel execution logs and ring buffers for unverified memory allocation panic messages or kernel oops events. - Enforce strict container runtime security policies and isolate exposed network interfaces using zero-trust microsegmentation.
Kernel network stack defense demands rapid security patch application and strict edge packet filtering to ensure enterprise Linux hosts remain protected against unauthenticated memory corruption exploits. #CodeDefence #Linux #Kernel #Fragnesia #CISA #KEV #IPv6 #RCE #CloudSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Active zero day exploitation targets SonicWall SonicOS SAML authentication bypass flaw CVE-2026-120050
item.description:
Perimeter security advisories published today warn of active wild attacks targeting enterprise remote access gateways. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit single sign-on logic errors to bypass multi-factor authentication controls and hijack corporate VPN sessions.
The security advisory covers SonicOS firmware vulnerability CVE-2026-120050 affecting SonicWall Gen6 and Gen7 firewall appliances. Remote threat actors send malformed SAML authentication responses containing manipulated cryptographic assertions to bypass single sign-on authentication handlers. Exploitation allows unauthenticated adversaries to gain administrative SSL VPN access to internal corporate subnets without presenting valid credentials. Threat intelligence feeds track automated scanning arrays actively weaponizing exposed management interfaces worldwide. Vendor updates mandate immediate deployment of firmware release builds 7.1.3-7020 and 6.5.4.15-116n.
Subverting secure remote access controllers destroys perimeter network boundaries across enterprise environments. Because SonicWall firewalls manage corporate SSL VPN access and site-to-site IPsec tunnels, an unauthenticated SAML authentication bypass permits threat actors to hijack user sessions, inspect internal network transit traffic, and move laterally across production subnets.
- Upgrade SonicOS firmware installations immediately across Gen6 and Gen7 firewalls to maintenance builds 7.1.3-7020 or 6.5.4.15-116n. - Audit SAML identity provider configuration logs for anomalous single sign-on authentication assertions originating from unverified IP ranges. - Restrict public internet access to firewall management interfaces, placing administrative portals on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Invalidate active remote access user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across VPN user accounts.
Perimeter firewall controller defense demands immediate firmware patch application and rigid identity provider verification to ensure corporate remote access gateways remain insulated from authentication bypass exploits. #CodeDefence #SonicWall #SonicOS #SAML #AuthBypass #SSLVPN #PerimeterSecurity #NetworkSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: Ivanti issues emergency security patches for critical Connect Secure zero day RCE vulnerability CVE-2026-124982
item.description:
Enterprise gateway maintainers have distributed out-of-band security fixes addressing an actively weaponized remote code execution vulnerability across secure access appliances. Remote unauthenticated adversaries exploit input parsing subroutines to obtain root execution on edge network gateways.
The emergency security update addresses Ivanti Connect Secure ICS and Policy Secure IPS vulnerability CVE-2026-124982 carrying a CVSS score of 9.9. The defect involves command injection flaws within web management API endpoints. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit crafted HTTP POST requests containing embedded command strings to execute arbitrary system code with root privileges. Threat research writeups confirm nation-state actors actively exploit the zero-day to drop web shells, exfiltrate active session tokens, and bypass internal multi-factor authentication controls. Vendor bulletins urge immediate patch application across all deployed appliance versions.
Subverting central remote access controllers undermines perimeter security boundaries and enterprise data confidentiality. Because Ivanti Connect Secure manages corporate VPN access and zero-trust remote connections, an unauthenticated root compromise allows threat actors to intercept internal transit traffic, harvest active user session keys, and access sensitive corporate assets.
- Apply official Ivanti security updates immediately across all deployed Connect Secure and Policy Secure gateway appliances. - Run the official Integrity Checker Tool ICT to detect unauthorized system file modifications or backdoor webshells. - Restrict public internet access to gateway administrative web interfaces, routing management access through out-of-band VLANs. - Invalidate active remote user sessions and reset corporate user authentication tokens across managed gateway nodes.
Secure access gateway defense requires emergency patch application and rigorous file integrity monitoring to ensure perimeter remote connections remain protected against unauthenticated command execution exploits. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #ConnectSecure #PolicySecure #ZeroDay #RCE #CommandInjection #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA
